extracted.intended_audience: Emergency managers, first responders, public information officers, elected/appointed officials, and partner agencies (federal, state, tribal, local, private-sector, and NGOs) who require NIMS/ICS training
extracted.subtask_description: Official county guidance describing the purpose and components of NIMS/ICS and the required/recommended training courses and prerequisites for various audiences (elected officials, first responders, supervisors, mid-level managers, command staff, and public information officers).

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS purpose and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS is a comprehensive, national approach to incident management that is applicable at all jurisdictional levels and across functional disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is intended to: Be applicable across a full spectrum of potential incidents, hazards, and impacts, regardless of size, location or complexity; Improve coordination and cooperation between public and private entities in a variety of incident management activities; Provide a common standard for overall incident management. Consistent application of NIMS lays the groundwork for efficient and effective responses and enables diverse entities to readily integrate and establish unified command during an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between NIMS and the National Response Framework (NRF)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIMS and NRF are companion documents designed to improve the Nation's incident management and response capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIMS provides the template for management of incidents regardless of size, scope or cause, while the NRF provides the structure and mechanisms for national level policy of incident response. Together they integrate capabilities and resources of various jurisdictions, disciplines, NGOs, and private-sector into a cohesive national framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS Components
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS Components link together and work in unison to form a comprehensive incident management system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIMS Components include: Preparedness; Communications and Information Management; Resource Management; Command and Management; Ongoing Management and Maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who NIMS applies to
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS is applicable to State, tribal and local governments, private sector organizations, critical infrastructure owners and operators, nongovernmental organizations and other organizations with an active role in emergency management and incident response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elected and appointed officials who make jurisdictional policy decisions must understand their emergency management roles and responsibilities to better serve their constituency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must take NIMS/ICS training
rubrics_metrics.description: All Federal, State, Tribal, and Local entities, Private Sector and Nongovernmental personnel with a direct role in emergency management and response must be NIMS and ICS trained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes all emergency services related disciplines such as EMS, hospitals, public health, fire service, law enforcement, public works/utilities, skilled support personnel, and other emergency management response, support and volunteer personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required baseline NIMS-compliant online courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Below are the new NIMS compliant courses that follow NIMS guidelines: IS-100.b (Introduction to Incident Command System), IS-200.b (ICS for Single Resources and Initial Action Incidents), IS-700.a (National Incident Management System (NIMS), An Introduction), IS-800.b (National Response Framework, An Introduction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: Any of the versions of these courses are considered equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-29: Public Information Officer Awareness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended for Tribal, Local and State public information officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-703.a: NIMS Resource Management Course
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended for government, private-sector, and nongovernmental organization individuals and teams who are charged with working together in a network to manage resources during domestic incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-706: NIMS Intrastate Mutual Aid - An Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: IS-706 - NIMS Intrastate Mutual Aid, An Introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended for State, local, and tribal emergency response and coordination personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-2200: Basic Emergency Operations Center (EOC) Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: IS-2200 - Basic Emergency Operations Center Functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended for Federal, state, local and tribal emergency managers; first responders to include incident commanders from all emergency management disciplines; private industry personnel responsible for coordination activities during a disaster; and Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster (VOAD) personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required classroom-only advanced ICS courses and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: IS-400 (G400) - Advanced Incident Command and IS-300 (G300) - Intermediate Incident Command are required, classroom-only courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerequisites for IS-400: IS-100, IS-200, IS-300, IS-700, IS-800. Prerequisites for IS-300: IS-100, IS-200, IS-700, IS-800.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements for Entry Level First Responders & Disaster Workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience includes Emergency Medical Service personnel, Firefighters, Hospital staff, Law Enforcement personnel, Public Health personnel, Public Works/Utility personnel, Skilled Support Personnel, and other emergency management response/support/volunteer personnel at all levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These personnel are listed under the federal/state/local/tribal/private sector & NGO training requirements; they must complete the applicable required NIMS/ICS courses for their role (see baseline and recommended courses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required training for First Line Supervisors
rubrics_metrics.description: First line supervisors, single resource leaders, field supervisors and other emergency management/response personnel who require a higher level of ICS/NIMS training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: Public Information Officers: FEMA IS-702a National Incident Management Systems (NIMS) Public Information Systems; FEMA IS-700B NIMS An Introduction; FEMA IS-706 NIMS Intrastate Mutual Aid - An Introduction; FEMA IS-800C National Response Framework (NRF) An Introduction; ICS-100 Introduction to ICS or equivalent; ICS-200 Basic ICS or equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required training for Mid-Level Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid-level management including strike team leaders, task force leaders, unit leaders, division/group supervisors, branch directors, and personnel of Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster (VOAD) and emergency operations center staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: Public Information Officers: FEMA IS-702a; FEMA IS-700B NIMS An Introduction; FEMA IS-703a NIMS Resource Management Course; FEMA IS-706 NIMS Intrastate Mutual Aid - An Introduction; FEMA IS-775 EOC Management and Operations; FEMA IS-800C NRF An Introduction; ICS-100 Introduction to ICS or equivalent; ICS-200 Basic ICS or equivalent; ICS-300 Intermediate ICS or equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required training for Command & General Staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Command and general staff, select department heads with multi-agency coordination system responsibilities, area commanders and emergency managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: Public Information Officers: FEMA IS-702a; FEMA IS-700 NIMS An Introduction; FEMA IS-703a NIMS Resource Management Course; FEMA IS-706 NIMS Intrastate Mutual Aid - An Introduction; FEMA IS-775 EOC Management and Operations; FEMA IS-800 National Response Framework An Introduction; ICS-100, ICS-200, ICS-300, ICS-400 (as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of course versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any of the versions of the baseline NIMS courses are considered equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly notes version equivalence for IS-100/200/700/800 (e.g., IS-100.b, IS-200.b, IS-700.a, IS-800.b) so different course iterations fulfill the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional training assets and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional training resources identified for completing required/recommended training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed assets include: US Fire Administration; Emergency Management Institute Training; SCEMD Training Resources (state courses for responders); SC State Fire Academy. Local contacts are provided for county-offered courses (NIMS and Training Coordinator contact info).
